chunks.text: Right now there's a zombie pressed up against my gate, and it's wearing my best friend's uniform.
The radio on his chest is about to tell every one of them exactly where I'm hiding.
An hour ago, I was basically the king of this mall. Let me back up.
I'm Danny. I do night security at Maplecrest Mall, and yeah, I've heard every mall cop joke there is.
I work nights for one reason. At three-fifteen every afternoon, I'm standing at the bus stop when my daughter Lily gets off.
She's seven, and she thinks I'm the king of the mall, because I carry forty-two keys, one for every store. Tonight, I'd only need one of them.
The job's pretty simple. I walk the loop, I rattle the gates, and around one a.m., Marcus calls me from down in the parking garage.
Marcus is twenty-two, he's studying to be a nurse, and he tells the worst jokes you've ever heard.
Tonight he calls at one-forty, and there's no joke. He's whispering.
[low, tense] Danny. There's a guy on the ramp. He's walking... wrong.
